title: Business Insights Application Insights: discovered apps, overlap, cost savings, All Applications and application details

prose.label: Overlapping Apps.
prose.text: {{overlap-users}} The terminology article defines the overlap differently {{divergence:overlap-users-definition}}. {{overlap-details-compare}} {{overlap-comparison-columns}} {{gap:contract-date-meaning}}
Scheduled reports for applications are in [[business-insights.reports]]; the product overview is in [[business-insights.overview]].

discovered-trend-thresholds.statement: The Discovered Apps tab of Application Insights charts, for the last 12 months, the number of high- and low-usage applications and newly discovered applications; high-usage apps have over 80% active users for the month compared to the total number of active users, and low-usage apps have less than 30%.

quotes: shows the trend for the number of high- and low-usage applications, along with the number of newly discovered applications for the last 12 months.
High-usage apps have over 80% active users for the month compared to the total number of active users.
Low-usage apps have less than 30% active users for the month compared to the total number of active users.

application-insights-tabs.statement: The Application Insights page is divided into three tabs: Discovered Apps, Overlapping Apps and Cost Savings; Discovered Apps lists the top 10 discovered applications.

quotes: is divided into three tabs:
View a list of the top 10 discovered applications.
The Overlapping Apps page (Analytics > Business Insights > Applications Insights > Overlapping Apps)
The Cost Savings page (Analytics > Business Insights > Applications Insights > Cost Savings)

engagement-index.statement: The Application Insights page defines Engagement Index as the percentage of active users in the last 30 days over the last 90 days for an app; the vendor's example of 50 active users in 30 days and 100 in 90 days gives 50%.

quotes: Engagement Index: The percentage of active users in the last 30 days over the last 90 days for an app.
if you have 50 active users in the last 30 days and 100 in the last 90 days for Box

engagement-index-with-plan.statement: The Business Insights terminology article says the Engagement Index calculation varies with metadata availability: with plan details it is active users in the last 30 days over purchased seats, falling back to assigned seats if purchased seats are unavailable and to the no-plan calculation if both are unavailable; with multiple plans the service shows the plan with the lowest engagement index.

quotes: This calculation varies based on the following metadata availability:
With Plan Details: The percentage of active users in the last 30 days over the number of purchased seats for an app.
If the data of the purchased seats is unavailable, the service replaces it with the number of assigned seats.
If both the data are unavailable, the service defaults to the preceding calculation performed for apps without plan details.
If multiple plans exist, the service shows the data for the plan with the lowest engagement index.

risk-index-definition.statement: In the legacy Business Insights All Applications page, Risk Index is the risk index assigned to the application, and this setting for the app is configured in the ZIA Admin Portal.

quotes: Risk Index: The risk index assigned to the application. This setting for the app is configured in the ZIA Admin Portal.

growth-trend.statement: Growth Trend is the percentage increase or decrease in user activity for every 30 days, calculated as the change in active users divided by the active users before the last 30 days, times 100.

quotes: Growth Trend: The percentage increase or decrease in user activity for every 30 days.
dividing the increase or decrease in the number of active users by the number of active users before the last 30 days, and multiplying it by 100

data-source-values.statement: The Application Details Data Source field names where usage was discovered: identity provider, Internet Access, connector integration or custom application signature, shown as IDP, ZIA, Connector or Custom ZIA.

quotes: Data Source: The source from where the application usage is discovered (i.e., identity provider (IdP), Internet Access, by connector integration, or custom application signature such as IDP, ZIA, Connector, or Custom ZIA).

multiple-entries-per-tenant.statement: Application Insights discovers app usage via the IdP, Internet & SaaS traffic, custom apps and direct connector configurations, so the same application tenant can appear in several entries with different Data Source values.

quotes: Business Insights discovers app usage via your IdP, Internet & SaaS traffic, custom apps, and direct connector configurations. Hence, you might see multiple entries for the same application tenant with different Data Source values.

cost-estimates.statement: Until costs are entered or edited, Application Insights shows Zscaler-estimated costs, which are underlined; the vendor describes them as conservative, based on enterprise premium plans with over 50% discounts, with greater discounts for larger deployment scale.

quotes: By default, when you use the service initially, applications have an estimated cost populated for them until you enter or edit the costs for the apps.
The Zscaler-estimated costs (Spend) are underlined.
These estimates are conservative and take into account the premium solutions of the SaaS providers (i.e., enterprise) with over 50% discounts, and also take the deployment scale into consideration.
The greater the deployment scale, the greater the discount.

cost-savings-table.statement: The Cost Savings tab lists the Top 50 Cost Savings Applications; Potential Savings is the opportunity from removing inactive users, with an asterisk marking savings based on Zscaler-estimated costs.

quotes: Top 50 Cost Savings Applications

Potential Savings: The potential cost-saving opportunity for the application by removing inactive users from the application. Cost savings for Zscaler-estimated costs are indicated with an asterisk (*).

efficiency-matrix.statement: The SaaS Efficiency Matrix places applications by license usage percentage and expense, and shows applications with greater savings opportunities in the bottom right of the graph.

quotes: View the SaaS Efficiency Matrix graph that shows the applications placement based on the license usage percentage and its expense to your organization
indicates applications with greater savings opportunities in the bottom right of the graph.

cost-savings-connector-or-skip.statement: Onboarding an application from the Cost Savings table that has connector integration support offers two options: configure an application connector, or skip it and set up subscription details using insights from other data sources (IdP or ZIA).

quotes: If you select an application that has connector integration support, the configuration page shows two options: either configure an application connector, or skip the connector configuration to set up the application subscription details and use the insights provided by other data sources (IdP or ZIA).

overlap-users.statement: On the Overlapping Apps tab, Overlapping Users for a capability is the number of users using at least one of the applications listed for that capability.

quotes: Overlapping Users: The number of overlapping users who are using at least one of the applications listed for the capability.

overlap-details-compare.statement: The Application Overlap Details page compares overlap metrics for up to 4 apps at a time and charts the weekly active user trend for each application.

quotes: You can compare the overlap metrics for up to 4 apps at a time
The User Activity graph shows the weekly active user trend for each application.

overlap-comparison-columns.statement: The Application Comparison table on the Overlap Details page shows the top 5 departments by app usage, spend in US dollars, and Contract Date as the date the app subscription ends.

quotes: Top 5 Departments: The top 5 departments by app usage.
Spend: The amount spent (in US Dollars) by the organization on the app subscription.
Contract Date: The date when the app subscription ends.

details-status.statement: The Status field on Application Details shows whether the application is onboarded to Business Insights and, for connector-integrated apps, whether the connector's API connection is valid or expired.

quotes: Status: The connection status between Business Insights and the application (i.e., whether the application is onboarded to Business Insights or not). For connector-integrated apps, the application connector's API connection is valid or expired.

details-users-table.statement: The Application Details Users table filters by the last 30, 60 or 90 days (last month, 2 months or 3 months for the ZIA table), defaults to Active Users, and can be searched by email address; the active vs. inactive graph can be filtered for the last 30 days or 12 months.

quotes: Select the time frame for viewing the data from the last 30, 60, or 90 days (last month, 2 months, or 3 months for the ZIA table).
By default, Active Users is selected.
Search for a specific user by their email address.
You can filter this tab for information for the last 30 days or 12 months.

details-users-table-by-source.statement: Which of three Users tables the Application Details page shows depends on the data source: Internet Access discovered or custom Internet Access apps, IDP discovered apps, or CONNECTOR apps.

quotes: one of the following Users tables appears:
For Internet Access Discovered or CUSTOM Internet Access Apps
For IDP Discovered Apps
For CONNECTOR Apps

details-m365-obfuscated.statement: For Microsoft 365 the Application Details User field shows obfuscated data by default; usernames require enabling settings in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

quotes: If you're viewing application details for Microsoft 365, the User field shows obfuscated data by default. To view usernames, enable the settings in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

licensing-insights.statement: The Licensing Insights tab shows unused licenses, potential cost savings and assigned vs. active users; the page says the Assigned Seats information is only applicable for a connector-based datasource, and the data can be filtered for the last 30 days, month or 2 months.

quotes: Unused Licenses: The number of unused licenses.
Potential Cost Savings: The potential cost saving opportunity by managing your licensing posture.
Assigned vs. Active Users: The graph shows the comparison between assigned vs. active users.

Assigned Seats: The number of seats assigned to users from the purchased seats. Hover over the bar to view the number of assigned seats for each SKU. This information is only applicable for connector-based datasource.
You can filter the data for the last 30 days, month, or 2 months.

all-applications-sources-and-export.statement: The All Applications page lists apps discovered from identity providers, Internet & SaaS traffic, connector integrations and custom application signatures; its data can be downloaded as a CSV file and shown 15, 50 or 100 rows per page.

quotes: The list includes discovery from all the data sources like identity providers (IdPs), Internet & SaaS traffic, connector integrations, and custom application signatures.
Download the data on the page as a CSV file.
You can also select the number of entries you want to view on a page (15, 50, or 100 rows).

all-applications-columns.statement: On the All Applications page, ACV is the annual contract value of the application's subscription, and Top Departments lists departments with their active-user counts in ascending order for the last 30 days.

quotes: ACV: The annual contract value for the applications' subscription.
Top Departments: The top departments by app usage.
The departments are listed with the number of active users (in parentheses) in ascending order for the last 30 days of app usage.

overlap-users-definition.summary: The Application Insights article counts Overlapping Users as users of at least one of the applications listed for a capability, while the terminology article defines Overlapping Apps as users using multiple apps with similar capabilities.

quotes: Overlapping Users: The number of overlapping users who are using at least one of the applications listed for the capability.

positions.says: Overlapping Users are users of at least one of the applications listed for the capability.

quotes: Overlapping Apps: Users using multiple apps with similar capabilities.

positions.says: Overlapping Apps are users using multiple apps with similar capabilities.

overlap-users-definition.impact: Whether an overlapping user uses one or several of a capability's apps is not settled, so the Overlapping Users count may or may not require more than one app.

users-table-columns.title: Which columns belong to which Application Details Users table
users-table-columns.detail: The page lists the columns flat after the three table headings (IDP, Internet Access or custom, CONNECTOR), so which columns belong to which table (for example Total Bytes and Transactions, or License Type) is not stated per table.

risk-index.title: What the risk and compliance data and the Risk Index scale mean
risk-index.detail: The legacy All Applications and application details pages say Risk Index is assigned to the app and configured in the ZIA Admin Portal, but the captured articles do not describe the Risk Index scale or the risk and compliance data, and the filter list's Sanction Status and Alternatives are not defined.

contract-date-meaning.title: Whether the Overlap table has a contract start date
contract-date-meaning.detail: On the Overlap Details page Contract Date is the date the subscription ends, while the Application Insights table has a separate Contract Start Date column; the Overlap table lists no start-date column, and no source says why.
